bands.name: Lateral (temporomandibular) ligament
bands.mechanical_role: the TMJ's main functional ligament; limits posterior and inferior displacement of the condyle, protecting the retrodiscal tissue
bands.function_note: The primary capsular reinforcement and functionally the most important TMJ ligament -- its oblique fiber orientation limits the mandible's condyle from over-retruding, protecting the vascular/neural retrodiscal tissue behind the disc.
bands.source: Bag AK, Gaddikeri S, Singhal A, Hardin J, Wadhwa V, Chen J, Guillerman RP (2014) 'Imaging of the temporomandibular joint: an update.' World J Radiol 6(8):567-582 -- TMJ capsular/accessory ligament anatomy and imaging correlation.

bands.name: Sphenomandibular ligament
bands.mechanical_role: an accessory ligament, largely non-functional as a direct joint restraint but developmentally significant
bands.function_note: A remnant of Meckel's cartilage (the embryonic first pharyngeal arch cartilage) rather than a true joint capsule derivative -- an accessory ligament lying medial to the joint, not directly contributing much mechanical restraint despite its consistent presence. This embryological detail is standard anatomy/embryology-textbook content (Moore's Clinically Oriented Anatomy, Langman's Embryology); the cited TMJ imaging review's own focus is disc position and pathology rather than embryology, so it is credited here only for the TMJ disc/capsular anatomy claims, not this specific developmental fact (attribution narrowed after adversarial fact-check, see docs/VERIFICATION.md).
bands.source: Bag AK, Gaddikeri S, Singhal A, Hardin J, Wadhwa V, Chen J, Guillerman RP (2014) 'Imaging of the temporomandibular joint: an update.' World J Radiol 6(8):567-582 -- TMJ capsular/accessory ligament anatomy and imaging correlation.

bands.name: Stylomandibular ligament
bands.mechanical_role: an accessory ligament, a thickened band of deep cervical (parotid) fascia rather than a true articular capsule derivative; limits excessive mandibular protrusion
bands.function_note: Widely regarded as a specialized condensation of investing cervical fascia rather than a true capsular ligament, separating the parotid and submandibular salivary gland spaces as a secondary anatomical role -- also standard gross-anatomy content credited to general references (Gray's/Moore's) here rather than to the cited TMJ imaging review specifically (attribution narrowed after adversarial fact-check, see docs/VERIFICATION.md).
bands.source: Bag AK, Gaddikeri S, Singhal A, Hardin J, Wadhwa V, Chen J, Guillerman RP (2014) 'Imaging of the temporomandibular joint: an update.' World J Radiol 6(8):567-582 -- TMJ capsular/accessory ligament anatomy and imaging correlation.

function: The TMJ's true capsular (lateral/temporomandibular) ligament plus two accessory ligaments of largely fascial/developmental rather than primary-restraint significance.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Bag AK, Gaddikeri S, Singhal A, Hardin J, Wadhwa V, Chen J, Guillerman RP (2014) 'Imaging of the temporomandibular joint: an update.'
